paper.title: Transformer-generated atomic embeddings to enhance prediction accuracy of crystal properties with machine learning
paper.research_summary: This paper proposes a novel atomic embedding strategy called universal atomic embeddings (UAEs), generated by a custom-built CrystalTransformer model based on the Transformer architecture. The embeddings—termed ct-UAEs—are designed as transferable atomic fingerprints to improve the accuracy of deep learning models (e.g., CGCNN, ALIGNN, MEGNET) in predicting crystal properties such as formation energy and bandgap. Experiments across multiple databases (Materials Project, JARVIS, MC3D, hybrid perovskites) demonstrate consistent accuracy improvements (e.g., 14% MAE reduction for formation energy on MP with CGCNN) and strong transferability. Interpretability analyses—including UMAP clustering, reverse prediction of elemental properties, and multi-task embedding similarity—reveal that ct-UAEs capture physically meaningful atomic features correlated with chemical stability, electronic behavior, and magnetism.

tasks.task_name_raw: Generate universal atomic embeddings (UAEs) for crystal property prediction
tasks.objective: To generate transferable, physics-informed atomic embeddings that serve as improved atomic fingerprints for enhancing the prediction accuracy of crystal properties across diverse deep learning models and material databases.
constraints: must be transferable across databases and back-end models
must capture complex atomic features without relying on predefined atomic attributes
must support rotational and translational invariance
output_goal: dense, low-dimensional tensor representations (ct-UAEs) for each atom in a crystal, capturing its role and interactions within the material

evidence.text: Here, we proposed an atomic embedding strategy called universal atomic embeddings (UAEs) for their broad applicability as atomic ﬁngerprints, and generated the UAE tensors based on the proposed CrystalTransformer model.

We developed the home-made CrystalTransformer model to generate universal atomic embeddings called ct-UAEs based on transformer architecture, which learns a unique “ﬁngerprint” for each atom, capturing the essence of their roles and interactions within the materials.
To construct universal atomic embeddings, the vanilla transformer algorithm is introduced as the main part of the model, resulting in the home-made model named CrystalTransformer

stages.stage_goal: Acquire large-scale, high-quality crystal structure and property datasets for training and evaluation.

evidence.text: To examine the atomic embeddings tensors obtained from different models, we used MP and MP* dataset for formation energy (Ef) and PBE bandgap (Eg), which are key properties for evaluating their chemical stabilities and electronic performances. MP stands for the 2018.6.1 version for MP44 dataset, which contains 69,239 materials with properties. MP* denotes the 2023.6.23 version, which contains 134,243 materials.

The ability and transferability of the universal atomic embedding are further tested on different databases and tasks. Each is cut into 8:1:1 for training, validation, and testing. Details on the dataset can be found in Supplementary 2A. As for the Jarvis dataset49, the result is shown in Table 1.

After merging two distinct datasets of HOIP materials69,70, we created a more diverse dataset containing 2103 HOIP crystals, which is still small compared to other material databases such as the MP dataset44.

stages.stage_goal: Convert raw crystal data (CIF files) into structured inputs suitable for the CrystalTransformer model, including one-hot atomic encoding and coordinate augmentation.
stage_output: batch × N × L one-hot atom matrix A
batch × N × D coordinate matrix X

evidence.text: When given an atom input in a batch of size batch for N-atom with L features per atom (L denotes a one-hot encoding of the atomic species) and the coordinate input with batch × N × D size (Here D indicates the spatial dimension (equals 3 in this context)), the model first topologically augments the coordinates input using translation and rotation transformation.

A0 = AW A + bA,
X0 = XW X + bX,
where A denotes the one-hot initialization for atom input features, with the dimension of batch × N × L. Tensor X denotes the atom position coordinates, with the dimension of batch × N × D.

stages.stage_goal: Train the CrystalTransformer model on crystal property prediction tasks (e.g., formation energy, bandgap) to learn task-agnostic atomic embeddings.
stage_input: target properties (Ef, Eg, total energy, total magnetization)

evidence.text: Front-end models as CrystalTransformer, CGCNN, ALIGNN, and MEGNET are ﬁrst pre-trained on the expanded MP* dataset, focusing on the bandgap energy Eg and formation energy Ef predictive tasks.
The CrystalTransformer method exhibits a theoretical complexity primarily driven by the self-attention mechanism in its Transformer layers.

stages.stage_name_raw: Evaluate ct-UAE transferability and accuracy gain
stages.stage_goal: Quantify improvement in downstream property prediction accuracy when integrating ct-UAEs into various back-end models (CGCNN, ALIGNN, MEGNET) across multiple datasets.
stage_input: target property labels (Ef, Eg, E, magnetization)
stage_output: MAE/R² metrics for each model-dataset combination

evidence.text: By performing experiments on widely-used materials database, our CrystalTransformer-based UAEs (ct-UAEs) are shown to accurately capture complex atomic features, leading to a 14% improvement in prediction accuracy on CGCNN and 18% on ALIGNN when using formation energies as the target, based on the Materials Project database.

stages.stage_name_raw: Select optimal number of clusters for element interpretability
stages.stage_goal: Determine the most appropriate number of atomic clusters (e.g., 3 or 4) via quantitative clustering validation to enable physically meaningful element categorization.

evidence.text: To determine the best number of clusters for atoms, the elbow plots56 and siltouette coefﬁcient graphs56 are needed, with quantitative analysis shown in Fig. 3b, c. Both elbow plot and silhouette coefﬁcient graph demonstrate that 3 or 4 clusters’ solution is the best choice for the classiﬁcation of atoms.

stages.stage_name_raw: Validate physical interpretability via reverse prediction and similarity analysis
stages.stage_goal: Confirm that ct-UAEs encode physically meaningful atomic properties by training CatBoost to predict elemental properties and measuring DTW similarity across multi-task embeddings.
stage_input: elemental properties (atomic radius, boiling temperature, etc.)
stage_output: DTW similarity regions and inverse distance curves (Fig. 4)

evidence.text: To further investigate the intrinsic information of the embeddings, we conduct reverse training experiments, which involves taking a series of important elemental properties, including atomic radius, boiling temperature, melting temperature, electrical conductivity, ﬁrst ionization energy as training targets to train a Catboost model66.
We use the Dynamic Time Warping (DTW)68 method to measure the similarity between mean embedding from MT@2p, MT@3p and MT@4p.
